exact_Guide_excerpt: - **Social security.** Contributions linked to pay that a treaty exempts in Germany (the § 32b(1) no. 3 case) are not special expenses (§ 10(2) sentence 1 no. 1 EStG; BMF letter on Vorsorgeaufwendungen, Rn. 199), unless the pay was earned in an EU or EEA state or Switzerland and that state allows no deduction for them (§ 10(2) sentence 1 no. 1 (a) to (c)). Contributions on foreign pay of the months before arrival or after departure (the no. 2 case) are not settled here (see Not yet confirmed). Swiss AHV contributions do not reduce the amount added for the rate (H 32b). Social security itself: de-social-contributions.

exact_Guide_excerpt: The person is taxed as a resident on their German income: Grundfreibetrag, special expenses, the EUR 36 lump sum and the resident deductions apply. Income that is not subject to German tax is left out of the base but raises the rate (progression, § 32b(1) no. 5 EStG): the tax rate is found on taxable income plus that foreign income, then applied to taxable income alone. Splitting needs § 1a. Foreign capital income is a special case: § 2(5b) EStG keeps capital income under § 32d(1) out of "income" wherever the law refers to it, and whether foreign interest or dividends of a § 1(3) applicant count in the 90% test and in the progression is not settled here (see Not yet confirmed).

exact_Guide_excerpt: - **Base:** the member's whole economic capacity, not only profit: capital and letting income count too. The base is at least EUR 1,318.33 a month and at most the ceiling of EUR 5,812.50 ([§ 223(3) SGB V](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__223.html)). If the spouse is not in a statutory fund, the spouse's income can count, less set amounts for children (§ 240(5)).

bindings.reviewer_exact_boundary: Saxony Midijob care-contribution allocation is not supplied. The actual outside-Saxony two-base algorithm is supplied and independently checked through de-payroll, closing the earlier general Midijob referral.
bindings.reviewer_exact_why_material: This is an ordinary employee population in one Land, not a hypothetical specialist intersection.

exact_Guide_excerpt: **Transition band.** Normal wage tax by the ELStAM. Contributions are worked out on reduced bases by two formulas in [§ 20(2a) SGB IV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_4/__20.html), with AE the monthly pay, G = EUR 603 and F = 0.6619. Base for the total contribution: BE = F x G + (2,000 / (2,000 - G) - G / (2,000 - G) x F) x (AE - G). Base for the employee's share: BE = 2,000 / (2,000 - G) x (AE - G). For the ordinarily shared branches outside Saxony, compute the total contribution by applying half the contribution rate to the first base, rounding to cents and doubling; compute the employee's ordinary half-rate contribution on the second base, rounding to cents. The employer bears the difference. Calculate the employee-only childless care surcharge on the first base; calculate care reductions on the second base, each rounded separately ([§ 1(2) and § 2(2) BVV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/beitrvv/__2.html)). At AE EUR 1,000 the 0.6-point childless surcharge is EUR 5.12, not EUR 3.41. Saxony has a separate allocation under § 58(5) SGB XI; this ordinary half-rate worksheet does not supply that Saxony allocation. At AE EUR 1,000 the bases are EUR 854.06 and EUR 568.36. Not for apprentices. Exactly EUR 2,000 is still in the band ("nicht übersteigen").

bindings.reviewer_exact_boundary: The new20% regular-return denominator's leave/sickness treatment, continuing homeoffice agreement/ordinance interaction, homeoffice-only failure case and actual euro conversion of Swiss pay remain unresolved.
bindings.reviewer_exact_why_material: Ordinary commuters can cross the20% gate and every CHF salary needs a supported euro input. The independently stipulated EUR-only salary example does not settle either.

exact_Guide_excerpt: - **Regular return, new from 2026.** There is a regular return only if the employee travels from home to the place of work and back on at least 20% of the agreed working days in the calendar year (protocol no. 5(b)). Agreed working days are those in the contract. Protocol no. 5(d) takes leave and sick days out of the working days for the 60-day test; the protocol does not say whether they also come out of the base for the 20% test, so check both bases (Example 2 passes and fails the same way on either).

- **Home office days.** Under the consultation agreement of 15 and 18 July 2022 (BMF letter of 26 July 2022), a working day spent entirely at home in the residence state is not a non-return day. That agreement was made under the treaty as amended in 2010; whether it still applies under the 2026 protocol is not confirmed (see the end of this skill). Either way, a home office day is not a day on which the person travels to the place of work and back, so from 2026 it counts against the 20% regular-return test.

Not yet confirmed: whether the home office consultation agreement of July 2022 still applies under the 2026 protocol text (it was made under the treaty as amended in 2010, and the new protocol no. 5 does not mention home office days; the 2023 Gre-1 notes still cite it); whether the BMF has issued an introductory letter on the 2026 commuter rules (none found in a search of bundesfinanzministerium.de on 2026-10-23); whether leave and sick days come out of the base for the 20% test; how the German implementing ordinance KonsVerCHEV (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/konsverchev/), which still uses 250 and 300 usual working days for part-time workers (§ 9) and a one day a week or five days a month return test (§ 7), sits beside protocol no. 5 from 2026; the euro conversion rule for Swiss pay; how the German tax office treats a year in which the 20% test fails only because of home office days.
